name.text: 01. Lesson 1.1: The PAGE API - Layout State Engine

questiontext.text:
[SLIDE: The PAGE API State Architecture]
[CONTENT_START] • DEFINITION: Central manager for the current page state, managing headings, contexts, and asset arrays. • ARCHITECTURE: Implemented natively in PHP OOP via the global $PAGE instance variable. • CODE IMPLEMENTATION: global $PAGE; $PAGE->set_context(context_system::instance()); $PAGE->set_heading("Welcome to ThemeAPI Masterclass"); $PAGE->add_body_class('themeapi-custom-view'); • TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensures theme engine methods output body classes accurately. • STRATEGIC TANGENT: Dynamically inject status-lockdown classes for learning plan tracking paths. • ASSIGNMENT: Inject a custom class hook into the page framework layout files. [CONTENT_END]
[NARRATIVE: Welcome to the structural foundation of Moodle application development. The Page API manages the comprehensive state of your rendering request. By explicitly calling the global PAGE object, setting its security context boundary, and mutating heading and class properties, we build a predictable canvas for our custom layouts and themes to sit on top of.]

name.text: 02. Lesson 1.2: The DML API - Single-Metric Optimization

questiontext.text:
[SLIDE: DML API - Dashboard Counter Optimization]
[CONTENT_START] • DEFINITION: Database neutral interface layer used to safely process structural entries. • PERFORMANCE RISK: Trainees load large, resource-intensive arrays into memory simply to run counts. • ENHANCED CALL: global $DB, $USER; $sql = "SELECT COUNT(id) FROM {user_enrolments} WHERE userid = :userid"; $enrollment_count = $DB->get_field_sql($sql, ['userid' => $USER->id]); • APPLICATION: Pass lightweight integer footprints directly into mustaches layout variables. • REFERENCES: Official Moodle DML manipulation reference guidelines. [CONTENT_END]
[NARRATIVE: Data efficiency dictates performance at scale. When rendering single metrics on a user dashboard header, bypass heavy multi-column lookups. Use the database manipulation layer to run counting aggregates natively inside the database, keeping memory consumption low and server responses lightning fast.]

name.text: 03. Lesson 1.3: The DML API - Analytical Data Restructuring

questiontext.text:
[SLIDE: DML API - Formatted Analytical Queries]
[CONTENT_START] • OPTIMIZATION SCHEMA: Fetch key-value read-models using menu variants to map data cleanly. • DATA TRANSFORMATION CODE: $data = $DB->get_records_menu_sql($optimized_sql, $params); arsort($data); // Keeps key values aligned $clean_score = round($user_avg, 1); • EXPLICIT SANITIZATION: Always use rules like AND finalgrade IS NOT NULL to shield data arrays. • INTERACTIVE SHIFT: Output associative structures to feed client-side chart.js components. [CONTENT_END]
[NARRATIVE: Data preparation is the core differentiator of high-performance analytics engines. By swapping multi-row structures for menu-driven associative reads, filtering empty null entries, and rounding decimal limits inside the query execution phase, your background engine feeds presentation charts clean, lightweight payloads without generating code execution bottlenecks.]

name.text: 04. Lesson 1.4: The DML API - Exception Architectures
05. Lesson 1.5: The DML API - Multi-Table Complex Analytical Joins

questiontext.text:
[SLIDE: Multi-Table DML Joins]
[CONTENT_START] • ANALYSIS GOAL: Link metrics across multiple tables to pinpoint operational risk. • COMPLEX JOIN STATEMENTS: $sql = "SELECT c.id, c.fullname, ROUND(AVG(gg.finalgrade), 2) as score FROM {course} c JOIN {grade_items} gi ON gi.courseid = c.id JOIN {grade_grades} gg ON gg.itemid = gi.id GROUP BY c.id, c.fullname ORDER BY score ASC"; $lowest_courses = $DB->get_records_sql($sql, null, 0, 5); • SCHEMATIC VALIDATION: Enforce UNI keys on targets to protect database calculations. [CONTENT_END]
[NARRATIVE: True learning analytics require robust multi-table execution patterns. By joining system course tracking maps cleanly against internal calculation grades, we compile targeted, performant profiles that power the low-performance reporting charts inside the plugin system.]

name.text: 06. Lesson 1.6: The DML API - Core Validation Bypass Mechanisms

questiontext.text:
[SLIDE: Low-Level DML System Fallbacks]
[CONTENT_START] • SYSTEM ENFORCEMENT: Completely bypass persistence structures when transaction layers lock up. • OVERRIDE COMMAND CONFIGURATION: $inserted_id = $DB->insert_record('competency_framework', $framework_object); • COMPETENCY SCALING FUTURE: Generates massive automated structures without memory leakage. [CONTENT_END]
[NARRATIVE: High-level persistent object APIs are the standard operational rule, but enterprise-scale automated systems demand robust fallback logic. By using raw insertion operations when cache limits or transaction validation sequences lock up, we establish resilient configuration points that secure long-term platform capability.]
